doc: The 1871 city's horse railways (T-3806): the track centrelines (`rails`; the renderer lays two strap rails on each, flush with the paving) on every street a source gives a line, and the four double-track lines the cars run (`services`), each a closed run out on the right-hand track and back on the other with a crossover at each stub, and a car every `headway_s`. Each section cites its sources; the grades are the route's (where the line ran) and the track's (single or double, and the turnouts).
corridor_line_why: The tracks lie on the context city's drawn street centrelines (data/context/1871.json streets), the lines the roadway ribbons are laid on.
gauge_basis: No source read gives the Chicago companies' gauge; 4 ft 8 1/2 in, the gauge of the Troy-built cars' eastern street railways, is reconstructed.

rail.kind: strap rail on longitudinal timbers, flush with the paving
rail.basis: Andreas vol. 2 p. 121: on Clark Street 'the first railway was laid, by spiking the rails to the planks, an additional thickness of plank being placed in the horse-path'; the flat rail's width and colour are reconstructed.

livery_basis: No source read for this ticket gives the companies' colours. Each company's car is painted in the manner of the period's Troy-built closed cars (a light body, a darker dash and lower panel, the company's name on the letter board), one colour per company so the three lines read apart: reconstructed (L-1871-horse-railways-3806).

car.basis: A closed four-wheel horse car of the 1860s of the Troy builders' pattern (Andreas: the first car came from Eaton, Gilbert & Co. of Troy): a body about sixteen feet long with open platforms and dashboards at both ends, a clerestory roof with a row of deck lights, seven windows a side, the company's name on the letter board, on two axles. Its dimensions, the pair of horses, the driver standing on the front platform and the conductor on the back one, and its pace of about five miles an hour are reconstructed (L-1871-horse-railways-3806).

hours.service_hours_basis: No source read gives the 1871 hours of service; the cars run from half past five in the morning to midnight (reconstructed).
hours.fire_basis: On the night of the fire no car runs from ten o'clock Sunday night, and none on the Monday. Andreas vol. 2 p. 706, of the Saturday night's fire on the West Side: in Clinton Street near Adams 'were half a dozen isolated street-cars, utterly unable to get back to their stables' for the crowd; p. 747: on the Monday 'the street cars, which had been run up there for safety' stood at Graceland; p. 753 and Colbert and Chamberlin p. 389: after the fire the rails of Clark Street were 'warped and twisted ... forced up ... two feet above the ground'. The hour the service stopped on Sunday night is reconstructed.

sections.name: State Street line, Lake Street to Twenty-second Street

sources.locator: City Railway and Omnibus Routes, printed p. 53

sections.note: Colbert and Chamberlin: rails 'on State from Lake Street south to the city limits'; Edwards: cars from State and Randolph 'via State to 22d, every minute'. Double track is inferred from the one-minute headway (Andreas: single with turnouts as first laid in 1859).

sections.name: State Street south of Twenty-second, to the city limits
sections.note: Andreas: cars to the city limits by June 1859. Single track with turnouts is reconstructed.

sections.name: Twenty-second Street, State Street east toward Cottage Grove Avenue

sources.locator: City Railway and Omnibus Routes, printed p. 53

sections.note: Andreas: the track 'extended, on Twenty-second Street and Cottage Grove Avenue' in 1859; Edwards: cars to Cottage Grove av. and Douglas place every four minutes. The context plan does not carry Cottage Grove Avenue, so the track stops at the plan's end of Twenty-second.

sections.name: Archer road line, State Street to Bridgeport

sources.locator: City Railway and Omnibus Routes, printed p. 53

sections.note: Andreas: 'a branch track was laid upon the Archer road from State Street' in 1864, completed to Bridgeport; Edwards: Archer road cars every eight minutes.

sections.name: Randolph Street line, State Street to the western limits

sources.locator: City Railway and Omnibus Routes, printed p. 53

sections.note: Edwards: cars from State and Randolph 'along Randolph to Robey, every five minutes, and to western limits every five minutes'. The plan does not name Robey Street; the track runs to the plan's end of West Randolph. Double track is reconstructed.

sections.name: Madison Street line, State Street to the western limits

sources.locator: City Railway and Omnibus Routes, printed p. 53

sections.note: Edwards: cars 'westward along Madison, every five minutes'; Colbert and Chamberlin: rails 'on Madison west'. How the Madison cars reached State and Randolph is not stated: here they turn back at State Street (reconstructed). Double track is reconstructed.

sections.name: Blue Island Avenue line, to Twelfth Street

sources.locator: City Railway and Omnibus Routes, printed p. 53

sections.note: Andreas: cars 'running to Twelfth Street by December 22, 1863'; Edwards: cars for Blue Island av. every six minutes. How they reached it from Madison or Randolph is not stated and is not drawn.

sections.name: Milwaukee Avenue line

sources.locator: City Railway and Omnibus Routes, printed p. 53

sections.note: Andreas: the Milwaukee line opened June 1864; Edwards: cars every ten minutes. Its extent in 1871 is not stated; the track runs the plan's length of the avenue (reconstructed).

sections.name: Clinton Street line, Randolph to Van Buren

sources.locator: City Railway and Omnibus Routes, printed p. 53

sections.note: Edwards: cars 'for Clinton south to Van Buren, Van Buren westward to Wood' and 'for Clinton and Jefferson to C. B. & Q. R. R. depot'. Where Clinton's track began is not stated: from Randolph here (reconstructed).

sections.name: Jefferson Street line, Randolph to Van Buren

sources.locator: City Railway and Omnibus Routes, printed p. 53

sections.note: Edwards: cars 'for Clinton and Jefferson to C. B. & Q. R. R. depot' every twelve minutes; Andreas: the Clinton and Jefferson lines opened October 1864. The extent is reconstructed.

sections.name: Van Buren Street line, Clinton westward to Wood

sources.locator: City Railway and Omnibus Routes, printed p. 53

sections.note: Edwards: 'Van Buren westward to Wood'. The plan does not name Wood Street; the track stops at 1800 west, where Wood Street runs (reconstructed).

sections.name: Clark Street line, Lake Street to Division Street

sources.locator: City Railway and Omnibus Routes, printed p. 53

sections.note: Andreas: the North Chicago company's Clark Street line from North Water Street, 'laid double to Division Street'; Colbert and Chamberlin: 'on north Clark Street from the river'. Edwards' cars 'leave city limits for Lake': the run across the Clark Street bridge to Lake Street is inferred from that.

sections.name: North Clark Street, Division Street to Fullerton Avenue
sections.note: Andreas: 'beyond that, a single track to Fullerton Avenue'. The turnouts are reconstructed.

sections.name: Division Street and Clybourn Avenue line

sources.locator: City Railway and Omnibus Routes, printed p. 53

sections.note: Andreas: 'From Clark Street west, on Division, to Clybourn Avenue, and thence on Clybourn Avenue to city limits', completed 1859.

sections.name: Chicago Avenue line, Clark Street to the North Branch

sources.locator: City Railway and Omnibus Routes, printed p. 53

sections.note: Andreas: 'West on Chicago Avenue ... to the North Branch', completed 1859; Edwards: cars for Chicago av. every fifteen minutes. Authorized from Rush Street; built from Clark here (reconstructed).

sections.name: Larrabee Street line, north from Chicago Avenue

sources.locator: City Railway and Omnibus Routes, printed p. 53

sections.note: Andreas: 'a single, or double, track on Larrabee Street, from Chicago Avenue to Little Fort road' (1864); Edwards: cars from 'corner Larrabee and Center'. The plan carries Larrabee only to Division Street, where the track stops.

not_laid.why: Andreas vol. 3 p. 164: 'two and one-fifth miles of double track on Wells Street from Randolph to North Clark, by November, 1875' was built after the fire.

Edwards: cars 'for Sedgwick' and from 'cor. N. av. and Sedgwick'; Andreas: the Sedgwick line of 1861. The context plan carries Sedgwick Street only south of Division, so the line north of Division is not drawn.

sources.locator: City Railway and Omnibus Routes, printed p. 53

not_laid.why: Not on the context plan; Twenty-second Street's track stops at the plan's end.
Andreas pp. 120: the company deferred Clark Street for ten years from 1860, the Michigan Southern holding it below Harrison; no line is in the 1871 timetable.

services.basis: Edwards' 1871 timetable: a car a minute from State and Randolph to Twenty-second; the cars that ran on to Cottage Grove Avenue and the Archer road share it here. They turn back at the Lake Street end of the track (Colbert's rails 'from Lake Street') and at Twenty-second.

sources.locator: City Railway and Omnibus Routes, printed p. 53

services.basis: Edwards' 1871 timetable: two services every five minutes, so a car about every two and a half minutes. They turn back at a stub in Randolph Street at State (reconstructed).

sources.locator: City Railway and Omnibus Routes, printed p. 53

services.basis: Edwards' 1871 timetable: every five minutes. They turn back at a stub in Madison Street at State (reconstructed).

sources.locator: City Railway and Omnibus Routes, printed p. 53

services.basis: Edwards' 1871 timetable: cars every twelve minutes to the city limits, to Sedgwick and to Clybourn and Larrabee, and every fifteen to Chicago avenue, all up Clark Street: about one every three minutes. Run here between Lake Street and the end of the double track at Division (the single line beyond carries no car in this scene).

sources.locator: City Railway and Omnibus Routes, printed p. 53
